overview.title: Find the right fit
overview.subhead: Every eye is different. We scan, measure and talk you through every option — then recommend what's safest for you.
overview.intro_text: Refractive treatments reduce your need for glasses or contact lenses. Some reshape the cornea with a laser; others place a thin lens inside the eye. Most are day procedures done with numbing drops. They can correct short-sightedness (myopia), long-sightedness (hyperopia) and astigmatism.
suitable: A stable prescription for at least a year
not_suitable: A prescription that is still changing

screening.title: Healthy eyes for the whole family.
screening.text: Not everything needs surgery. Our optometrists and specialists also look after everyday eye health — from a first check-up to long-term care.

list.name: ZEISS SMILE® pro 3.0

list.seo_description: ZEISS SMILE® pro 3.0 at Optimax: flapless laser vision correction with about 8–10 seconds of laser time per eye and recovery in 24–48 hours.

card.summary: Our newest flapless laser. About 8–10 seconds per eye.

hero.title: ZEISS SMILE® pro 3.0
hero.title_line2: Seconds of laser. Years of clear vision.
hero.subhead: Our newest flapless laser vision correction, powered by the ZEISS VisuMax® 800. A tiny 2 mm opening, no flap, and most people are back to light activity in a day or two.

what.title: What is ZEISS SMILE® pro 3.0?
what.text: A flapless procedure that reshapes the cornea from the inside to correct short-sightedness and astigmatism. The laser creates a thin disc of tissue (a lenticule), which your surgeon removes through a tiny opening. Treatment is planned with ZEISS VISULYZE software using your own eye data.
features: No flap and no blade — gentle on the cornea
Quiet, contactless docking for more comfort
Lower risk of dry eyes than traditional LASIK
Backed by 13 years and 32,000+ SMILE treatments at Optimax

suits: Anyone wanting a flapless alternative to LASIK
not_suits: Very thin corneas or severe dry eyes

compare.title: SMILE® pro vs SMILE vs traditional LASIK

steps.note: Numbing drops only — no general anaesthetic.

items.title: Eye preparation

items.title: Laser application
items.text: The VisuMax® 800 shapes a thin lenticule inside the cornea and a tiny opening.

items.title: Lenticule removal
items.text: Your surgeon removes the lenticule through the micro-opening, reshaping the cornea.

items.title: Healing begins
items.text: No stitches. The opening seals naturally and vision settles over the week.

hero.title: ZEISS SMILE®
hero.subhead: A flap-free laser vision correction trusted by surgeons worldwide. One small opening, no flap, and most people get back to routine within one to three days.

what.title: What is ZEISS SMILE®?
what.text: SMILE stands for Small Incision Lenticule Extraction. It corrects short-sightedness and mild astigmatism by reshaping the cornea through one small opening. Because there's no corneal flap, there's less disruption to the eye and a lower risk of dry eyes than with LASIK.

suits: Anyone who prefers a flap-free option
People worried about dry eyes after LASIK
Those wanting a quick return to routine

list.name: ZEISS PRESBYOND® 2.0
list.image_alt: Woman lifting her reading glasses to read her phone
list.seo_title: ZEISS PRESBYOND® Laser Blended Vision for presbyopia | Optimax
list.seo_description: PRESBYOND® Laser Blended Vision at Optimax helps people over 40 see near, intermediate and far with less reliance on reading glasses.

card.summary: Laser blended vision for near, middle and far.

hero.title: ZEISS PRESBYOND®
hero.subhead: A personalised laser treatment for age-related reading difficulty. PRESBYOND® Laser Blended Vision helps you see near, middle and far — with less reaching for reading glasses.

what.title: What is PRESBYOND®?
what.text: From around 40, the eye's natural lens gets less flexible and close-up focus gets harder — this is presbyopia. PRESBYOND® gently tunes one eye for distance and the other for near, joined by a smooth 'blend zone'. Your brain combines the two for a wide, comfortable range of vision.
features: A wider range: near, intermediate and far
Planned around your eye dominance and vision profile

suits: Healthy eyes, with or without mild-to-moderate myopia, hyperopia or astigmatism
Anyone tired of switching between reading and distance glasses
People wanting a long-term laser solution
not_suits: Frequent dry eyes or unstable vision
Cataract, glaucoma or other eye disease
Thin corneas or previous corneal surgery

suits: Anyone wanting a precise, all-laser option

card.summary: Blade-free LASIK with two lasers. Treats a wide range.

hero.title: Femto-LASIK
hero.subhead: A proven LASIK treatment using two lasers for safe, accurate results — suitable for a wide range of prescriptions.

what.title: What is Femto-LASIK?
what.text: A bladeless evolution of classic LASIK. A femtosecond laser (Ziemer FEMTO LDV™) creates a thin, precise corneal flap, then an excimer laser (SCHWIND AMARIS®) reshapes the cornea to correct your prescription.
features: Intelligent eye tracking and fast treatment
Treats a wide range of prescriptions

suits: Anyone wanting a fast-recovery laser option
not_suits: Thin corneas or irregular corneal shape
Chronic dry eye or eye inflammation
list.not_suits_note: If Femto-LASIK isn't right, ZEISS SMILE® or TESA may be.

list.name: TESA®
list.image_alt: Smiling diver with mask, free from glasses
list.seo_title: TESA® TransPRK surface laser in Malaysia | Optimax Eye Specialist
list.seo_description: TESA® (TransPRK) at Optimax: a no-touch, flap-free surface laser for thin corneas, dry eyes and active lifestyles.

card.summary: No-touch surface laser. Good for thin corneas.

hero.title: TESA®
hero.subhead: A surface laser alternative for active lifestyles and sensitive eyes — often an option when LASIK isn't, such as with thin corneas or dry eyes.

what.title: What is TESA®?
what.text: TESA (Transepithelial Surface Ablation, also known as TransPRK) uses one excimer laser to remove the thin surface layer of the cornea and reshape the tissue beneath — in a single step. No blade, no instruments touching the eye and no flap.
features: SCHWIND AMARIS® 1050RS excimer laser with eye tracking
No flap — so no flap complications
Suitable for thin or irregular corneas
Great for active people and contact sports

suits: Not eligible for LASIK or SMILE due to corneal thickness
Dry eyes or a sensitive eye surface
Anyone wanting a non-invasive, flapless option
not_suits: A prescription that is still changing
list.not_suits_note: If TESA isn't right, ZEISS SMILE® or ICL may be.

list.seo_description: Advanced Surface Ablation (ASA, also called PRK or LASEK) at Optimax: flap-free, blade-free laser vision correction for thin corneas and active lifestyles.

card.summary: Flap-free surface laser. Keeps the cornea strong.

hero.title: ASA
hero.subhead: Advanced Surface Ablation is a flap-free laser treatment for people with thin corneas, dry eyes or active lifestyles — the treatment Optimax first offered in 1995.

what.title: What is ASA?
what.text: Also known as PRK or LASEK. The thin outer layer of the cornea is gently removed, then an excimer laser corrects your prescription on the surface. A soft protective lens supports healing. Because no flap is made, the cornea stays structurally strong.
features: Customised treatment from detailed corneal mapping

suits: People told they're not suitable for LASIK

list.name: Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL)
list.image_alt: Smiling diver with mask, free from glasses
list.seo_title: ICL — Implantable Collamer Lens for high myopia | Optimax
list.seo_description: ICL at Optimax: a removable lens for moderate to high myopia (-6.00D to -20.00D) and thin corneas. No tissue removed, porcine-free option available.

card.summary: A removable lens for high prescriptions.

hero.title: ICL
hero.subhead: A thin, flexible lens placed inside the eye — an alternative to LASIK for moderate to high short-sightedness and thin corneas. No corneal tissue is removed.

what.title: What is an ICL?
what.text: A micro-thin, flexible lens made of collamer — a biocompatible material. It sits behind the iris and in front of your natural lens, correcting myopia and astigmatism without changing the shape of the cornea. It's invisible, needs no maintenance, and can be removed or replaced.
features: Suitable for thin or irregular corneas

suits: Not eligible for LASIK or PRK
list.not_suits_note: Over 45? PRESBYOND® or FLACS may be a better fit.

list.name: RGP lenses
list.seo_title: RGP lenses for keratoconus & irregular corneas | Optimax
list.seo_description: Custom-fitted Rigid Gas Permeable (RGP) lenses at Optimax: sharp, stable vision without surgery for keratoconus, irregular astigmatism and high prescriptions.

card.summary: Custom-fitted lenses. Clear vision without surgery.

hero.title: RGP lenses
hero.subhead: Custom-fitted Rigid Gas Permeable lenses for sharper, steadier vision — especially for irregular corneas, keratoconus and people who aren't suited to laser.

what.title: What are RGP lenses?
what.text: Contact lenses made from an oxygen-permeable material, so your cornea can still breathe. Because they hold their shape, they create a smooth optical surface over irregular corneas — giving sharper, more stable vision than soft lenses.

suits: People unsuitable for LASIK or other laser
Anyone wanting a non-surgical, reversible option
not_suits: Can't adapt to rigid lenses after a trial period

list.name: FLACS cataract surgery
list.seo_title: FLACS laser-assisted cataract surgery in Malaysia | Optimax
list.seo_description: Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Cataract Surgery (FLACS) with the Ziemer Z8 at Optimax, plus monofocal, bifocal and trifocal lens options.

card.summary: Laser-assisted cataract surgery and premium lenses.

hero.title: FLACS
hero.subhead: Femtosecond Laser-Assisted Cataract Surgery — a bladeless, computer-guided way to remove cataracts, with a choice of lenses planned around how you live.

what.title: What is FLACS?
what.text: A cataract is when the eye's natural lens turns cloudy, usually with age — making vision blurry, glary and dim. FLACS uses the Ziemer Z8 femtosecond laser to make the key steps of cataract surgery bladeless and computer-guided, for more precision and predictability.
features: Less ultrasound energy — gentler on the eye
Every step monitored in real time

suits: Glare or halos, especially at night
Cataract affecting daily life, reading or driving
not_suits: Suitability is confirmed through a full clinical evaluation
Some eyes are better suited to conventional surgery — your specialist will advise

steps.title: Precise at every stage.
steps.note: Local anaesthesia with no injections. General anaesthesia available if needed.

items.title: Corneal incision
items.text: The laser creates a precise entry point.

items.title: Capsulotomy
items.text: A perfectly centred opening is made in the lens capsule.

items.title: Lens fragmentation
items.text: Laser pulses soften the cataract, so less ultrasound is needed.

items.title: New lens
